title: Shapes and cells
description: The shapes of the puzzle, their cells, the tool tabs' operations, the status window, the 3D drawing mesh and the grid editor's layer drawing. Editing shapes is refused while a solve runs (invalid_state, decision 0011); an edit of a shape removes the solutions of the problems that use it.

shape.get.summary: A shape with its non-empty cells (of one layer, when asked).

layer.description: Only the cells with this z (the grid editor's XY plane; the cube editor's XZ and YZ planes are the client's: filter the cells by y or x).

shape.create.summary: Adds an empty shape at the end: of a size in cells, or of the grid's default size. On a stacking puzzle a disc of size 1 (the original's New), and no size may be given (invalid_argument).

shape.duplicate.summary: Adds a copy of a shape at the end.

shape.delete.summary: Removes a shape; the problems drop it.

shape.move.summary: Moves a shape to a place in the list; labels renumber. On a sliding puzzle the boards stay above the pieces (a move across them is refused, invalid_argument), the boards are numbered by place again, and the starts and goals follow; a stamped piece moved past the 255th place (a mark is a byte) loses them, told in document.changed.notice.

shape.rename.summary: The shape's name (empty for none). On a sliding puzzle a start/goal shape's name is the user's part (its board number stays; the name 'Board n' it shows without one, or its problem's 'Board n - Start / Goal', leaves it empty), its problem is named after it, and a piece's name may not begin with "sg:" or "__sggoal:" (invalid_argument).

shape.setWeight.summary: The weight: heavier shapes stay in place when taken apart.

shape.setColor.summary: The shape's own color, or null for the default one.

shape.setImage.summary: Lays a picture over the shape's bounding box, upright, on a sliding puzzle (decision 0038): on a piece, or on a board (a start/goal shape), whose floor shows it under the pieces; new image bytes (a PNG or JPEG, at most 8192 pixels a side) or one the puzzle has, by its number. The picture then turns, flips and moves with the cells; it takes the place of the ones the shape had. Refused (invalid_argument) on other grids, for a shape without cells, bytes that are not such a picture, or a part that misses it.

data.description: The image file, base64. Give this or 'image'.

image.description: A picture the puzzle has (ShapeImage.image). Give this or 'data'.

src.description: The part of the picture shown, in its pixels.

border.description: The picture of the tray's border (decision 0046) instead of the shape's own: laid over the whole tray and shown on its border. A board only (invalid_argument otherwise). Default false.

shape.setImages.summary: Lays a stack of pictures over the shape's bounding box (decision 0047), the bottom one first, in place of the ones it has: one undo step, none when nothing differs; an empty list takes them off. Each is as for shape.setImage; all share the box, and turn, flip and move with the cells together. Refused (invalid_argument) as shape.setImage is, and for more than 16 pictures.

layers.description: The pictures, the bottom one first.

border.description: The pictures of the tray's border (decision 0046) instead of the shape's own. A board only. Default false.

shape.clearImage.summary: Takes the shape's pictures off, or with 'border' the pictures of its tray's border (nothing changes when it has none).

border.description: The border's picture instead of the shape's own. Default false.

shape.setBorder.summary: Changes the border of a sliding puzzle's board (decision 0046): whether its tray shows one, its corners, its material, its thickness and its color. Only the fields given change; one undo step. Refused (invalid_argument) for a shape that is no sliding puzzle's board.

thickness.description: 0 for a thin rim, else the rim's width in voxels.

color.description: The border's own color, or null for none.

shape.imageData.summary: A picture of the puzzle: its file, which the client decodes and keeps by its hash (the snapshot carries only the number and hash).

shape.setCells.summary: Applies a tool to cells, each with the mirror and span options (the grid editor); cells outside the space or not cells of the grid are left out. Several calls inside edit.begin / edit.end are one undo step. Refused (invalid_argument) on a stacking puzzle, whose shapes are discs (stacking.setDiscSize).

color.description: The color put on the cells; absent: none (the shape's own).

shape.setBox.summary: The same for every cell of a box, corners included, clamped to the space (the box selection's fill and clear). Refused (invalid_argument) on a stacking puzzle, whose shapes are discs (stacking.setDiscSize).

shape.resize.summary: Sets the size in the editor's units (engine.info's sizeUnit); shrinking drops cells outside. With toAll the other shapes grow by as much (they never shrink). Refused (invalid_argument) on a stacking puzzle, whose shapes are discs (stacking.setDiscSize).

shape.taskSet.summary: The tool tabs' operations the document's grid offers, in the original's button order. The sliding grid leaves out what would give a shape more layers (the nudges along Z, the turns about X and Y, double, triple, the grid scale), as the original grayed them out.

toAll.description: It can be applied to every shape at once.

shape.task.summary: A tool tab operation on a shape (and, with toAll and a task that allows it, on every shape): flip, rotate, nudge (refused when cells would leave the grid), prune, center, to origin, minimize, double, triple, fill holes, the surface. Refused (invalid_argument) on a stacking puzzle, whose shapes are discs (stacking.setDiscSize).

changed.description: The shape changed at all (cells, size or hotspot).

cellsChanged.description: Cells whose state or color changed (fill holes: the holes filled).

shape.taskPreview.summary: The mesh (as shape.mesh, the drawing style) the shape would have after shape.task, worked out on a copy: nothing changes. The client draws it as a ghost over the shape while the pointer is on a tool tab button. The same refusals as shape.task (a nudge out of the grid is invalid_argument), but allowed while solving.

shape.info.summary: The status window's row for one shape, with its status line.

shape.table.summary: The status window: a row per shape, in list order.

shape.mesh.summary: The shape's mesh as the original's 3D view drew it, as a binary frame: in its own orientation, or turned by a transformation of the grid (a Placement's), which is how an assembled solution, a placement of the assembly explorer or a position of the movement explorer is drawn: the mesh of the piece's transformation, at its cell minus the turned shape's hotspot (MeshFrame.hotspot). Allowed while solving.

transformation.description: A number of the grid's symmetry table, mirrors included (bricks 0 to 47); absent or 0 is the shape as it is. Beyond the table: invalid_argument.

grid.geometry.summary: The grid editor's drawing of one layer of a space of the document's grid (at most 65536 cells a layer): each cell's outline (a circle on the sphere grid) and the cell across each edge. Units: a cube 1 by 1, prism triangles of side 1, spheres 1 apart, rhombic 5 by 5 cells and tetrahedra-octahedra 3 by 3 cells to 1 by 1.

neighbors.description: Per edge (corner i to i + 1): the index in cells of the cell across it, -1 for none.

grid.neighbor.summary: The cell across a side of a cell, in a space of the document's grid (the 3D view's tools that add a cell at a face): the sides are numbered as a MeshFrame's voxelFace (Voxel::getNeighbor, faces). Null when the cell across is outside the space. A cell outside the space or not a cell of the grid, or a side the cell does not have: invalid_argument.

cell.description: The cell across the side, or null when it is outside the space.

changed.description: Cells changed; 0 leaves no undo step.
